site.title: Harold Young — Human Posts
site.description: Writing about systems, consciousness, and the spaces between humans and machines.

canonical.note: All canonical URLs point here. Cross-posted platforms receive this as rel=canonical.

toolbar._position_note: Where the graph's controls sit. bottom (default): the bar along the bottom (undo, redo; the layout, cluster or ring; the dimensions; Reset; More, with the view actions). top: no bottom bar; they join the top bar after its pages and links and before the gear, as icon buttons the height of the pills: undo, redo, Reset, and a menu (an hourglass) with each dimension as a checkbox row (one on at a time), the bucket size when the one on has it, the view actions (Zoom to fit, Unpin all, Reset sizes) and, when show.layout is on, the layout as a row. The menu's heading is dimensions.groupLabel. The top bar then keeps to one row: when it does not fit, the source pills after the first shrink to their dot, then a page or link with an icon shows the icon alone, then the first pill's text gives way to an ellipsis. In the art state of a cover they are there but take no taps until the graph rests. show: history, layout and dimensions each on unless set false.

browser.label: Browser (Web Speech API)
browser._voices_note: Only these English voices are offered, in this order, and only the ones the reader's device has: at most maxVoices, or one English fallback if none match. A device voice matches a name exactly or by prefix.
browser.cost: free — the device already has it, no key, no network

gemini.label: Google Gemini
gemini.cost: billed per character to whoever owns the key
gemini._exposed_note: Off in the picker on purpose. Turning this on bills a real account for every paragraph anyone reads. Set exposed true only for a build where the reader owns the key.

tts._note: available = the engine ships in the build and may be turned on. exposed = it appears in the reader's engine picker. An engine that costs the listener money, or needs a key they do not have, stays available and unexposed: present for whoever wants it, invisible to everyone who was handed this and should not be billed for reading.

theme.name: default
theme._name_note: default (the original dark look) or sketchbook (paper and pencil: warm off-white paper in light mode, graphite paper in dark, hand-drawn hulls, edges and card outlines, titles in a handwriting face shipped as fonts/NothingYouCouldDo-Regular.ttf with its SIL Open Font License). A viewer can choose the other theme, and the sketchbook's light or dark mode (else it follows the device), in the panel.
theme._timeOfDay_note: Off unless set. true, or { enabled, transitionSeconds (4), seasonTint (0.1), hemisphere ('north'), palettes: { <time>: { dark: [top, bottom], light: [top, bottom] } }, seasons: { winter, spring, summer, autumn }, text, quiet }. When a piece is selected or open, the page background fades to the palette for its scene.time_of_day (dawn, morning, midday, afternoon, dusk, evening, night, late-night), tinted by the season of scene.date. The default palettes keep text at WCAG AA in both modes. A piece's scene (time_of_day, date, place) is read from its text's front matter, else its frontmatter.json (scene object or top-level fields). The reader can turn it off in the panel.

reader._note: How the reader pane presents a piece. Engine defaults keep the old reader.

header._note: kicker: an optional small line above the title, a list of parts joined with separator (default " — "). Tokens: {n} the piece's number, {n_words} it in words, {N_words} capitalized, {book} site.title, {author}, {title}. A part whose token has no value is left out. byline: "by <author>" under the title, default true.

reader._progressBar_note: top (a bar along the top edge of the reader, default), side (down its right edge), or none.
reader._allowDownload_note: Whether the reader offers Export (download the piece as a markdown file). Default true.
reader._fonts_note: The faces offered for the text in the panel. default is the page's own face (Atkinson Hyperlegible) and is always offered. opendyslexic ships as fonts/OpenDyslexic-Regular.woff2 next to the page, with its SIL Open Font License in fonts/OpenDyslexic-OFL.txt; it loads only when chosen.

graph._note: Visual parameters for the graph. Here rather than in the code so they can be tuned without a rebuild, and so a fork can look different without editing components. Not all of these are exposed in the interface, and they do not need to be — being reachable is the point.

timeAxis._dock_note: left | right | top | bottom. The axis is a ruler pinned to the edge of the viewport, not an object in the canvas: panning and zooming the corpus moves the corpus past it, the way a ruler stays put while the paper slides under it. A docked edge also decides the direction — a side rail runs earliest at the top, a top or bottom rail earliest at the left.

graph._collapseGesture_note: tap (default) or doubletap: what opens and closes a container, on its title or its closed node. A tap is under 4px of movement; more than that drags the container. With tap, a double-tap on a title zooms like anywhere else; with doubletap, it toggles the container instead.
graph._doubleTapMs_note: A double-tap or double-click anywhere on the graph (canvas, hull, card, title) zooms in about 2x at that point and opens nothing; shift+double-click, or a double-tap with two fingers, zooms out. A single tap waits this long (ms) to be sure it is not the first of two, then opens the card or toggles the title.
graph._layoutVersion_note: Part of the key the reader's saved positions are filed under, with the layout's name and the settings that shape it (the spiral's mode, spacing, start radius and direction, the card size, the simulation). When any of those change, positions saved for the old arrangement are no longer read back and the layout places the nodes afresh; bump this to do the same on purpose. Old positions stay in the browser until the reader uses Forget. Positions a reader dragged are retired with the rest. Default 1.

spiral._mode_note: path (default): a container's chapters sit one after another on a golden spiral, radius growing by the golden ratio each quarter turn, so each next edge is short. scatter: the golden-angle arrangement. Containers of containers place their children beside the first one, the label about a third of the way down.
spiral._spacing_note: Gap between neighbouring cards along the spiral, in px.
spiral._startRadius_note: The spiral's radius at the first chapter. null = about two thirds of a card.
spiral._direction_note: outward (default): the first chapter sits under the container's label and the spiral winds clockwise outward from it, so the last chapter is on the outer end. inward: the same reading order turned round, so the first chapter is on the outer end, at the top where a new reader looks first, and the spiral winds clockwise inward to the last one beside the label.
spiral._anchorEnd_note: Which part of a container's spiral sits on its anchor (containers.<id>.anchor). center (default): the spiral's centre, its title there and the first chapter just under it. outer: the spiral's outer end, its last chapter, sits on the anchor, and the spiral is turned so the first chapter lies from it toward openTowards.
spiral._openTowards_note: With anchorEnd outer, the direction from the last chapter (on the anchor) to the first: down (default), down-left or down-right. Set per container under containers.<id>.spiral.
spiral._keepBelow_note: crown: no card and no part of the hull of an anchored container goes above the roots' crown, the line opening.crownY (a fraction of the cover art's height). Where the spiral would cross it, it is turned (the least turn that clears it, up to a quarter turn) or else moved down; nothing is cut off. null (default): no line.
spiral._cardScale_note: The scale a container's cards are drawn at, and spaced for, against graph.card (default 1). A card keeps its text at every scale; the reader zooms in to read it. Set per container under containers.<id>.spiral, with spacing, anchorEnd, openTowards and keepBelow, each over the graph-wide value.

graph._initialFocus_note: What the first screen frames: all (default) or a container id. A container is framed so its cards are still cards (initialFocusMinScale, default 0.4); when the whole top-level container fits at that scale, it is framed instead. Zoom to Fit always frames everything.
graph._visibleLayers_note: Which edge layers draw lines: sequence, authored, tag, topology. Default sequence only. Containment is never a line; the hulls show it. A connected_to between two pieces that follow one another in a series is folded into that next edge.
graph._containerCount_note: Whether a container's title shows how many items it holds: the open container's label, the closed container's blob, and the source pill at the top. Default true.
graph._readingProgress_note: A thin bar along the bottom of each card shows how far this viewer has read it, filling as they go; a card read to the end keeps a full bar and a small tick. Kept in the viewer's own browser (viewState), never sent anywhere. Default true; false hides it.
graph._roots_note: true, or { seed }, to grow roots behind the graph: thin branching lines along the reading path, from the top container's title to each child's, to the first piece of each run and on along the sequence edges. A root reaching a piece draws in once the viewer opens it and thickens once they finish it (from their own reading progress). Seeded by seed, else the top container's id, so a book always grows the same roots. Drawn under the hulls, never takes a pointer; colour from --pp-root-color. Default false.
graph._containersStart_note: containersStart: closed or open, how containers start (and where Reset returns them). closed closes every container inside another (a book's acts; every container when none is inside another); open closes none. Unset: initialCollapsed decides ('all' or a list of container ids; none by default).
graph._links_note: Link nodes: an item whose front matter has link (or external_url, as JSON Feed items carry) and no body text. Its card shows its title, its subtitle (front matter subtitle) and its blurb (summary or blurb); a tap on the card, its corner arrow, or Enter follows the link, and the reader never opens for it. Its page (<id>.html) sends the visitor straight on. A JSON Feed item with external_url and no content is one too. newTab: external (default: a new tab for links off this site, the same tab for links on it), always or never. A site whose every item is a link node shows no reading groups in the panel (Reading, Listening, Your place).
graph._intro_note: A short text shown once under the title pill, on its own line in the top bar, for a site's bio line. A string is plain text (blank lines make paragraphs); { "text": "...", "format": "markdown" } is markdown, rendered when the site is built (links in it take taps). Off when empty.
graph._anchors_note: A container can rest on the cover's art: containers[<id>].anchor { x, y }, fractions of the art's width and height (settings.opening). With anchors and the cover on, the graph state rests at the home view (initialFocusMinScale, default 0.4, from the frame's corner) instead of the first framing, and a fresh layout, or Reset, puts each anchored container's centre (its title, or its closed node) on its anchor. Each anchored container keeps a frame of its own and stays pinned to its anchor: the anchor is its centre, closed or open, through every opening and closing, until the reader drags it; it then stays where it was dropped (kept across visits) until Reset. Zoom to Fit still frames everything. The anchors are part of the saved positions' key, so moving one retires positions saved against the old ones. containers[<id>].labelPosition: center (default, where the layout puts the title), top (centred at the top of the hull) or hidden (not drawn).
graph._initialScale_note: graph.initialScale { minCardWidthPx } (default 0, none): the first screen shows cards at least that many CSS px wide. With initialFocus a container, the first frame zooms in at least that far; when the container then does not fit, the frame is its top (a hanging container's anchor) and the rest runs off the bottom, for the reader to scroll and drag to. With anchors, it is the scale the graph state rests at (the larger of it and initialFocusMinScale), each anchor placed through it, so Reset comes back to it with every act on its anchor. Zoom to fit and the + and - keys zoom about the middle of the viewport, as before.
graph._containerLayout_note: How a container lays out its members: the golden spiral (default), or hang, chosen for every container by graph.containerLayout: "hang" or for one by containers[<id>].layout. A hanging container hangs from its anchor: the anchor is the top of its hull, and the members run below it in reading order as a chain at most hang.columns cards wide (default 2), each one card step from the one before, down the far side and back up the near side, so one end of the chain is low and the other at the top under the anchor. hang settings, in graph.hang for all or containers[<id>].hang for one: direction down (default; centred under the anchor, far side to the right), down-right or down-left (hung outward from the anchor, the hull's inner edge under it so nothing reaches back past it, for containers at the sides); firstAt bottom (default; the first member at the far, low end and the last at the top under the anchor) or top (the reverse); columns; gap (px between cards, default 12). The title sits in the far column's empty top when it fits there, scaled down to a card's width if need be, or else above the chain. The hull is the cards' outline padded by hull.padding (graph.hull.padding for all, containers[<id>].hull.padding for one; default half a card for a hanging container), and its top never rises above the anchor. Closed, the container is its pill centred on the anchor, drawn at graph.closedPillScale of its full size (default 1). containers[<id>].hull: false leaves a container's hull undrawn (a book whose acts and cover stand in for it); its title follows labelPosition as before. A container that holds containers is not hung; the containers in it are. All of these are part of the saved positions' key.
graph._zoomPivot_note: pointer (default): the wheel and a pinch zoom about the pointer and the fingers, the + and - keys and Zoom to fit about the middle of the viewport. art: every zoom (the wheel, a pinch, a double-tap, the keys, Zoom to fit, Reset's way back) is about one point on the cover's art, opening.zoomPivot, wherever the pointer is, so what sits round that point stays round it as the reader zooms in. A pan still moves the view. Without a cover, as pointer.
graph._zoomMode_note: geometric (default): a zoom enlarges the whole graph as one picture about the zoom's point (graph.zoomPivot), so anchored containers move apart and off their anchors. grow-in-place: with anchored containers (containers.<id>.anchor on a cover), each one is drawn larger or smaller about its own centre, which stays where the graph rests it, on its anchor on the cover's art, at every zoom (closed: its node grows; open: its hull, cards and title grow about its anchor, an outer-end spiral's last chapter staying on it); they are not moved apart. The wheel, a pinch, a double-tap, the + and - keys, Zoom to fit (each container grown until the first meets the screen's edge) and Reset all zoom this way, about the point under graph.zoomPivot where it is drawn now, so a pan made before a zoom is kept, not scaled; a pan still moves everything, the containers off their anchors. A zoom in stops where two grown containers, closed or open, would come within 16 px of each other (their boxes, each grown about its centre); opening a container while zoomed in past that zooms back out to it. Dragging a grown container moves it with the pointer. Whatever is not anchored zooms as before.
graph._closedPill_note: The closed pill's look. shape soft (default): the engine's own soft rounded shape, the same every time for the same container; blob: an irregular rounded shape (eight corners round an ellipse, nearly straight sides, soft corners), kept for a site that wants it. status false leaves the container's status line off it. labelSize: its label in px at full size (before closedPillScale); null: 1.6 of card.labelMaxFontSize. Its colours and its label's face are the container's look (_containerLook_note).
graph._containerLook_note: A container's own look, per container under containers.<id>, drawn on its closed node and its open hull alike: fill, a colour, at fillOpacity (0 to 1; unset, as given); stroke, the outline's colour (none for no outline; unset, the container's own colour on the closed node and the containment entry's stroke on the open hull); labelFace, a family the site's fonts carry, for the closed node's label and the open hull's title alike (measured in it); labelColor, both labels' colour, drawn as given. The closed node keeps its glow in its outline's colour (none in the sketchbook theme). The containment entry's own colours (badgeColor, color) stay its chapters' cards'. Without these, the engine's own look, as before.

dimensions._groupLabel_note: What the group of dimensions is called where a reader sees it: the label in the bottom bar and the heading in its More sheet. dimensions by default.
dimensions._labels_note: Rename any dimension wherever a reader sees it (the bottom bar and its tooltips): { "commits": "revisions" }, or { "commits": { "label": "revisions", "title": "..." } }. Ids: time, commits, narrative, chronology, and readers (the edge layer of readers’ connections, its own switch, off until turned on, shown only when there are any). Engine names unchanged by default.

_contributions_note: Readers' contributions, off unless a site sets "contributions": { ... }. Kept in their own file, never in feed.json or the text. src: the file, relative to the page (default ./contributions.json; copied from the site root when there). Each item: id, type (essay | comment | art | connection), author (a display name), created, status (only "approved" is shown), anchor { chapter (the piece's slug), and optionally exact, prefix, suffix: the passage it is about }, body (plain text, never HTML), title (an essay's), asset and alt (art: a png/jpg/webp/gif/avif path inside assetBase, default ./contributions/assets/), to (a connection's other chapter), test (true for test items). showTest (default false): show test items. Shown as a count on each card, a From readers section under the text, and connections as the readers dimension: a dashed edge layer, off until the reader turns it on. A passage that can't be found in the current text, or can't be told apart from a repeat, falls back to the chapter and says so. submit (default false): a form in that section to send one; endpoint (default ./api/contributions) is where it posts; limits { name 60, body 8000, exact 400 }.

opening._crownY_note: Where the roots' crown (the stem meeting the roots) is on the art, as a fraction of its height: the line graph.spiral.keepBelow crown keeps the anchored containers under. null: none.
opening._zoomPivot_note: { x, y }, fractions of the art: the fixed point of every zoom when graph.zoomPivot is art. null: none.
opening._fit_note: height (the default): the whole plant fits the screen's height in the art state. width: the plant (the art state's image above crownY) spans the screen's width, sideMargin px in from each edge, but never so large that the crown falls below the screen's foot (on a wide screen the plant is as large as keeps the crown on it); the roots run off the bottom and the rest of the art is reached by scrolling down into the graph state.
opening._returnAbove_note: crown: in the graph state a scroll up, or a drag down, anywhere above the roots' crown (the small plant, the title, the top bar) brings the art state back; below it the graph's own pan and zoom work as before. null: only at the top strip (grip).
opening._topBarInArt_note: The top bar (and its band, topBar.band) shows in the graph state alone, fading in over 200 ms as the page settles there; true keeps it in the art state too.

_opening_byline_note: byline.text is a same-tab link to byline.href. With a title over the cover it sits directly under the title in each state (under the art layout's last line in the art state, under the graph layout's one line at the crown in the graph state, moving between them with the page): its left edge at the last line's, its top gap (default 0.3) of the title's size below that line's baseline, in the title's face and colour, at size (default 0.25) of the title's size (its largest span), never under minSize px (default 0, no floor), at opacity.art (default 0.35) in the art state and opacity.graph (default 0.56) in the graph state (a single number for both). It stays a link in both states. case: lower (default) draws it in lower case, as-written as written. graphScale (0 to 1; default null): in the graph state the byline is that share of the graph layout's title size (its largest span), never set to a line's width there (title.fit), and its gap is of that size too; it moves between its art state size and this as the page moves; null: as in the art state. Without a title it sits centred under the art and fades out as the page moves to the graph, as before.
_opening_title_note: Optional: a title set over the cover, as text. art and graph are its two layouts, crossfaded with the images: lines, each { x, y, spans }, with x the line's left edge and y its baseline as fractions of the canvas's width and height, and spans, each { text, size, rise }, with size and rise (a lift off the baseline) as fractions of the canvas's width, so the title scales and moves with the art. font names a face (a site's own in fonts, below), followed by 'Arial Black', Impact, sans-serif; color defaults to the accent; opacity is the text's. text is its accessible name (default: the art layout's words). hideGraphTitle (default true) leaves the graph's own title for the whole book undrawn while the cover carries it.
_opening_backdrop_note: How strongly the art shows behind the graph. backdrop.opacity (0..1, default 1) is the graph state's roots at the zoom the graph rests at; zooming in they fade toward opacityZoomedIn (default 0.3), reached at zoomForFloor (default 2.5) times that zoom and held further in; zooming back out they return. keepAbove (a share of the canvas's height from the top, default 0) is the part of the graph state's image that keeps its own strength whatever the zoom, such as a small plant above the roots: it is drawn as a second copy of the image masked to that part, with a short soft seam. The earlier graph.artOpacity is still read as backdrop.opacity.
_opening_reach_note: Off by default. reach.enabled draws rootlets from the art to the containers: thin, seeded, forking lines in screen space, in one layer between the art and the graph. tips: points on the art, each { x, y } as fractions of its width and height (the root ends the rootlets grow from). Each container they reach for (those with an anchor, else each child of a top-level container) is reached from its perContainer nearest tips (default 3); a rootlet is aimed at the container's centre and stops stopShort px (default 18) before its outline, closed or open. When a container is dragged or the graph pans or zooms, the ends re-aim, easing over lagMs (default 600); the starts stay on the art. A rootlet draws in over drawMs (default 1800) the first time it shows. They fade with the backdrop's roots as the graph is zoomed in. Reduced motion: they appear without drawing in and follow at once. Anchors: containers[<id>].anchor { x, y }, fractions of the art, rests a container there in the graph state (see graph._anchors_note).
_fonts_note: A site's own faces: [{ family, file, license }], file and license relative to the site root (ttf, otf, woff or woff2). Copied next to the page, declared with @font-face and preloaded; nothing is fetched from elsewhere. A face whose file is missing is left out with a warning, and text set in it falls back.
_accent_note: Optional: one accent colour for the site in every theme (links, the reader's and the panel's accent, the bottom bar's active pill, the selected state). Kept as given wherever it reaches WCAG AA (4.5:1) for text, else moved toward black on paper or white on graphite just far enough; the tint behind an active control is the colour at 12%. Empty: each theme keeps its own.
_topBar_note: The top bar, in line with the source pills and the settings gear, in both states of a cover. pages: [{ id, label, hideFromGraph }], a button each after the pills that opens that item in the reader; id is the item's id or its slug (the last part of its url, without .html); label is the button's text. hideFromGraph: true takes the item out of the graph (its node and every edge to it), so the button is the way to it. icon (optional): an SVG body string on a 24-unit box (the markup inside <svg>, e.g. an Iconify body), drawn in the button at the pills' height; showLabel (default true) shows the label as text beside it, false the icon alone (the label stays its name). links: [{ id, label, href, icon, newTab, showLabel }], a button each after the pages that goes to href (the same tab, or a new one with newTab: true, rel noopener; http, https, mailto or a path on the site), showing icon with label as its accessible name and title, and label as text too when showLabel is true (default false; a link without an icon always shows it). When the row does not fit on one line (with toolbar.position top), a page or link with an icon shows the icon alone. subscribe: { action, method, field, label, icon, placeholder, thanks, error, newTab }, an email sign-up, off unless action is set (a path on the site such as /api/subscribe, or an https address): an icon button after the links (icon, else label as text; label its accessible name) opens a small sheet under the bar (a dialog; Escape or a tap outside closes it, the focus goes to the field) with one email field (placeholder), a submit button reading label, and a message line. A submit posts JSON { [field, default email]: the address } to action with method (default POST) and Content-Type application/json; on a 2xx reply the sheet shows thanks and clears the field, otherwise the reply's own error (a JSON { error }) if it has one, else error, and error when the request fails. This is the one request the engine makes on a reader's action, and only to the address the site set; nothing is sent on load. newTab: true sends the form the plain way instead (form-encoded, into a new tab), for a service with its own page. addFeed (default true): the + after the pills, for adding a feed; false leaves it out.
_opening_graph_note: opening.graph.artStateOpacity (default 0.6): the graph is never hidden; in the art state it hangs from the roots where it rests in the graph state (it moves with the art, so anchored containers stay at their anchors), at this strength, and comes up to full strength as the page moves to the graph. Only the top bar (the source pills, the top bar's pages, the gear) takes taps in the art state; the bottom bar fades in with the graph state.
_opening_grip_note: opening.grip.extra (default 16): in the graph state the grip that brings the cover back is the whole top strip, full width, from the screen's top down to the bottom of the top bar's row (the source pills, the pages, the controls in line with them, and the gear; not the intro under them) and this many px below it. The controls in the bar stay on top and keep their taps; a tap in the gaps between them, or a drag down from there (touch or mouse), brings the cover back. The grip's mark stays at the top centre as the hint.
_opening_top_note: opening.top: { art, graph }, px of space between the page's top controls (the source pills, the top bar's pages and the settings gear; the screen's top without them) and the plant's top edge, in the art state and the graph state. Where the plant starts in each state image is read off the image itself (its first row with ink). With art set the art state's art is as large as fits from there down (not centred); with graph set the graph state's plant sits there and graph.artOffset is not used. Unset (default): the art state centres the whole canvas and the graph state scrolls it up by graph.artOffset.
_opening_note: A cover as the page's top state, off by default. mode two-state (the only one): the cover art fixed behind the page, and the graph drawn over it. art: artState and graphState, two images of one canvas (the same size, the parts they share in the same place), stacked and crossfaded as the page moves, the art state's at 1 - p and the graph state's at p; or full alone, one image for both states; paths relative to the site root. In the art state the whole canvas fits the screen with byline.text under it (a same-tab link to byline.href); in the graph state it is scrolled up by graph.artOffset of its height (0.33 puts the place where the plant meets the roots about a quarter of the way down a phone) with its roots at backdrop.opacity (see _opening_backdrop_note), and the graph, hanging from the roots in both states (see _opening_graph_note), comes up to full strength over it while its bottom bar fades in. The art never pans or zooms with the graph. Scroll, a touch drag, a tap on the art, or ArrowDown, PageDown or Space go to the graph; ArrowUp or PageUp, a scroll up at the top edge, or the grip (the top strip, see _opening_grip_note) go back; a reader can scrub partway and it settles at one of the two over snapMs. alt describes the image. ground: dark (default) puts the art on the theme's dark paper and keeps the page in dark mode, the reader and the panel keeping the reader's own mode; paper puts it on the theme's paper; or an object for a night sky (a dark ground): { top, bottom, textureFrom, colorFrom, texture } — the base colour is top (default #050505) down to colorFrom (a share of the screen's height, textureFrom unless set) and runs to bottom at the foot (empty: the theme's dark paper); the paper's grain and fibres are absent above textureFrom (default 0.35) and come in toward the foot, the ground adding its own copy at texture strength (default 1, 0 for none) so they are stronger low. startOn: remembered (where this reader left it, the art for a new reader; Forget clears it), art or graph. A #read= link opens on the graph. Reduced motion: the two states swap in a short fade, with no scrolling.
_opening_title_fit_note: opening.title.fit width: each line that names a width (line.width, a fraction of the art's width) is set to that width once the title's face has loaded, its spans scaled together, and the byline is set to the width of the layout's last line, under it in each state.
_opening_graph_rootsFit_note: opening.graph.rootsFit width: in the graph state the art is scaled so the roots' widest row (below crownY on the graph state's image) spans the screen's width, or, on a wide screen, so the graph state's image from its small plant to its foot fits the height. The art moves and scales between the two states. With artStateOpacity 0 the graph is not drawn at all in the art state (display none, nothing to hit).
_topBar_band_note: topBar.band: { color }, a band the screen's width behind the top bar, from the screen's top to 8 px under the bar's row, drawn by the two-state cover (opening) and coming and going with the bar. null: none.
_opening_rootsVector_note: opening.art.rootsVector: an SVG of the graph state image's roots (one path per part of each edge of the roots' tree, as src/lib/rootsVector.js reads it: data-e, data-part, data-a, data-b, data-tip, data-loop, data-free, stroke, stroke-width; and circle data-tip for each tip), drawn in the graph state in place of the image's roots below backdrop.keepAbove. Each act's roots (containers.<id>.rootTips, tip names from the file; or else the tip nearest its anchor) bend toward it when it is moved: the last third of each root, eased in, its tip by the whole move, what grows off it moving with it. The rootlets (opening.reach) are not drawn for an act that has such roots. Empty: the image's roots.
_opening_rootsFollowMs_note: opening.art.rootsFollowMs (default 0): how far behind its act each act's vector roots follow it, in ms. The bend is driven by where the act is drawn on the screen at each frame (a closed act part way through any move it is easing over, an open one where its cards are), never by where it is going or by the pointer, and follows it as a critically damped spring with this time constant (it covers about 60% of a jump in that time and 95% in 2.4 times it, never overshooting), so the act moves first and its roots answer: when it is dragged, opened, closed, pushed clear of another, sent back by Reset, or zoomed. 0: the roots are where the act is drawn, at once. Reduced motion: at once.
